_why: Fed to Goblin Brain with `node "C:/Goblin Brain/scripts/teach.mjs" "C:/Find Aliens/docs/lessons/entity-index.teach.json"` from C:\xixoxis. lessons -> per-file rules Kenoma reads with the file; lore -> facts brain_lore serves.

lore.subject: research/extract-entities.mjs
lore.fact: research/extract-entities.mjs reads each page's data by slicing its last inline <script> up to the `// ---------- helpers` marker and running that in a vm sandbox whose `window` is the sandbox itself, so a page that keeps data on the browser global (blind-pool.html's `window.LEASES = [...]`) is read instead of throwing. `document` is deliberately absent, and an error in any one page still stops the whole run.

lore.subject: public/climate.html
lore.fact: public/climate.html is a 1 KB redirect stub to carbon-class.html, but research/extract-entities.mjs still lists `climate` in PAGES and not `carbon-class`, so the Carbon Ledger contributes no entities to public/data/entities.json and nothing warns about it.

lore.subject: public/data/entities.json
lore.fact: public/data/entities.json is regenerated by research/extract-entities.mjs, which indexes the site's own pages and does NOT approve connections: approved, sourced connections reach public/data/web.json only through `node research/review.mjs`, so a regenerated entity index is a diff for a person to read before it ships.

lore.subject: research/extract-entities.mjs
lore.fact: research/extract-entities.mjs reads Deep State from the generated public/js/deep-state-data.js (pageData special-cases it, as it already does for crash-conduits and crash-finance-data.js), not from the page, and flattens the dossiers to one item per CLAIM so a mention anchors on #DS-<dossier>-<item>, which deep-state.html routes to that claim and opens its record. Each claim's `sources` are dropped before the item is built, or strings() would sweep publisher names into the matched text and make the reporting outlet a subject of the story.

lore.subject: public/data/entities.json
lore.fact: When a page's structure changes, check the entity index's ANCHORS and not just its counts: deep-state and demystification went on serving 10 mentions pointing at #dossier-... ids that no longer existed on either page, so readers arriving from The Web scrolled nowhere. An index that can no longer read a page keeps the links it had when it could.

lore.subject: research/entities.seed.json
lore.fact: research/entities.seed.json carries several organisations under two ids each - SEC and Securities and Exchange Commission, US Department of Justice and U.S. Department of Justice, FDIC and Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation - which splits their mentions and makes a page swapping spelling look like a content change. They belong to one record with the other spelling as an alias; merging ids rewrites mentions across every page, so it is its own job.

lore.subject: research/extract-entities.mjs
lore.fact: GENERIC in research/extract-entities.mjs was dead from the commit that created the file (182d761): the characters either side of its group are literal backspaces (0x08), not the \b escape, so the regex required a backspace around the word and never matched. ROLE_WORDS on the next line is written correctly and is what it meant to be. Restored and extended, it drops 44 crowd labels that had been in the index all along (Enron investors, Holdout creditors, Workers and users of public services), each with one mention. A regex that never matches raises no error - test the pattern itself, and scan source for control characters.

lore.subject: research/extract-entities.mjs
lore.fact: research/extract-entities.mjs reads the compiled atlas from public/data/atlas-public.json (108 dossiers 1636-2026 and 8 lineages), which duplicates nothing: not one atlas code appears as an id in crash-conduits' data and the lineage names appear nowhere else on the site. A dossier's `participants` become the item's `who`; `citations` and `decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy` are excluded from matched text, the latter because it holds the claim the dossier exists to refute. Lineage chain entities are split on -> and / because a link names a step, not one body.

lore.subject: public/web.html
lore.fact: public/web.html places more labels than it has room for once the atlas is indexed: 221 names against 158, and entities on more than one page go from 54 to 124. Labels run off both edges and one collides with the DEMYSTIFY spoke name. The clipping predates the atlas (the shipped index already cut off Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation); fitK()'s 150px side margin and the greedy four-spot label placement were tuned for a sparser web.

lore.subject: tooling
lore.fact: Do not write a backslash escape through a quoted heredoc: `cat > f <<'EOF'` collapsed a doubled backslash-b into a 0x08 byte in the Python source it was writing, reintroducing the exact bug being fixed, and sed with | as its delimiter silently never matched. Build the character as chr(92), write from a script file on disk, and read the bytes back before believing the edit landed.
